title: Vacana literature (vacana sāhitya)
summary: The corpus of vacanas — short rhythmic Kannada prose-poems, usually closing with the author's signature name (aṅkita) for the Lord — composed by the twelfth-century śaraṇas of Kalyāṇa and by later vacanakāras. They teach devotion to Śiva as the liṅga, the six stages (ṣaṭsthala), the triad of guru, liṅga and jaṅgama, work as worship (kāyaka) and giving (dāsōha), and criticize caste, pollution rules, temple and Vedic ritualism and outward show in favour of lived experience (anubhava).

attribution.tradition: the utterances of the śaraṇas (Basava, Allama Prabhu, Akka Mahādēvi, Cennabasava and some two hundred others, women among them), preserved in palm-leaf bundles and carried to Uḷavi after the Kalyāṇa upheaval
attribution.scholarly: a twelfth-century core with later accretions; much of the corpus is known through fifteenth–sixteenth-century Vijayanagara-period anthologies

scholarly.text: 12th-c. core; later vacanakāras to the 17th–18th c.

structure.description: about 20,000 vacanas ascribed to more than 200 named vacanakāras, including over thirty women (counts differ between editions)

editions.name: Samagra Vacana Sāhitya, 15 vols., Government of Karnataka 1993 (general editor M. M. Kalburgi) — edition details to be confirmed in Phase C
P. G. Halakatti's vacana editions (from the 1920s)

notes: Vacanas are not numbered uniformly across editions; teachings from them are cited here by incipit. family 'vedic' follows the coverage-map grouping (A7, Vedic family); it does not settle the tradition's internal debate on Vedic authority (see dsp:virasaiva-veda-agama-authority).

title: Vacanas of Basavaṇṇa (Basavaṇṇanavara vacanagaḷu)
summary: Vacanas signed Kūḍalasaṅgamadēva: devotion and humility before devotees (dāsōha), sevenfold inner and outer purity ('do not steal, do not kill, do not lie…'), the body as the temple of the moving (jaṅgama) against the fixed (sthāvara) temple, compassion as the root of dharma, and the unity of all devotees regardless of birth.

structure.description: more than a thousand vacanas (count differs by edition)

notes: aṅkita (signature): Kūḍalasaṅgamadēva. Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Allama Prabhu
summary: Vacanas signed Guhēśvara, marked by paradox and enigmatic imagery (beḍagu) and by the teaching of the void (śūnya, bayalu); they criticize external observance, the pursuit of powers and attachment, and locate māyā in the mind's desire rather than in objects.

structure.description: commonly counted at about 1,300 (differs by edition; low confidence)

notes: aṅkita (signature): Guhēśvara. Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Akka Mahādēvi (Mahādēviyakkana vacanagaḷu)
summary: Vacanas addressed to Cennamallikārjuna as her only husband: bridal devotion, longing and union, the renunciation of worldly marriage, clothing and social shame, and equanimity under praise and blame.

structure.description: several hundred (commonly c. 350–430; differs by edition)

notes: aṅkita (signature): Cennamallikārjuna. Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Cennabasava
summary: Vacanas signed Kūḍalacennasaṅgamadēva, honoured in the tradition for their systematic exposition of the ṣaṭsthala path, the relation of liṅga and aṅga, and the eight shields (aṣṭāvaraṇa).

structure.description: among the largest single-author collections (count not recalled reliably)

notes: aṅkita (signature): Kūḍalacennasaṅgamadēva. Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Siddharāma
summary: Vacanas signed Kapilasiddhamallikārjuna by the Sonnalige builder-saint who in the tradition's account turned from public works to liṅga-devotion under Allama; they treat work, yoga and devotion.
notes: aṅkita (signature): Kapilasiddhamallikārjuna. Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Dēvara Dāsimayya (Jēḍara Dāsimayya)
summary: Vacanas signed Rāmanātha, reckoned by the tradition among the earliest; they speak of Śiva's gift of the world, of the devotee's work, and deny that the self is male or female.
notes: aṅkita (signature): Rāmanātha. Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Ambigara Cauḍayya
summary: Vacanas of the ferryman śaraṇa, signed with his own name; sharp criticism of hypocrisy, ritualism and pride of learning.
notes: aṅkita (signature): Ambigara Cauḍayya (his own name). Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Maḍivāḷa Mācayya
summary: Vacanas of the washerman śaraṇa remembered as the fierce defender of the community of devotees (gaṇācāra).
notes: Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Nuliya Candayya
summary: Vacanas of the rope-maker śaraṇa, remembered for insisting on the primacy of kāyaka.
notes: Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Āydakki Mārayya
summary: Vacanas of the rice-gleaner śaraṇa, signed Amarēśvaraliṅga, including the vacana that calls work (kāyaka) Kailāsa.
notes: aṅkita (signature): Amarēśvaraliṅga. Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Āydakki Lakkamma
summary: Vacanas of Mārayya's wife, remembered for teaching that kāyaka must not gather more than the day's need.
notes: Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Muktāyakka
summary: Vacanas of the woman śaraṇa who, grieving her brother Ajagaṇṇa, questioned Allama and was questioned by him; they treat grief, speech and silence, and realization.
notes: Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Satyakka
summary: Vacanas of a woman śaraṇa of humble occupation (remembered as a sweeper), affirming devotion over outward observance.
notes: Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Nīlāmbike
summary: Vacanas of Basava's wife, in which Basava appears as her spiritual guide.
notes: Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Vacanas of Ṣaṇmukhasvāmi
summary: Later (17th-c.) vacanas and songs arranged by the ṣaṭsthala scheme.
notes: aṅkita (signature): Akhaṇḍēśvara (low confidence). Cited by incipit; edition numbering to be fixed in Phase D.

title: Ṣaṭsthalajñānasārāmṛta
summary: A collection of about seven hundred vacanas by Toṇṭada Siddhaliṅga arranged under the six sthalas; the major fifteenth-century continuation of the vacana tradition.
notes: Count 'about 700' from memory (often given as 701); confirm in Phase C.

title: Karaṇahasuge
summary: A work ascribed to Cennabasava on the body, the senses and the inner instruments (karaṇa) and their relation to the liṅga — counted among the early Vīraśaiva yoga writings.
notes: Content summary reconstructed from general memory; verify.

title: Mantragōpya
summary: A short work on the secret of mantra and the liṅga, variously ascribed in modern lists (to Akka Mahādēvi, and in some accounts to Cennabasava).
notes: Attribution uncertain — the task brief listed it under Cennabasava; common lists give it to Akka Mahādēvi. Verify.

title: Yōgāṅga Trividhi
summary: A short poem in tripadi metre ascribed to Akka Mahādēvi on yoga and the path to the liṅga.

title: Śūnyasampādane
summary: A dialogic anthology that sets vacanas in a narrative frame centred on Allama Prabhu presiding at the Anubhava Maṇṭapa of Kalyāṇa: Allama examines and is examined by Basava, Cennabasava, Siddharāma, Akka Mahādēvi, Muktāyakka, Gorakṣa and others, so that each 'attainment of the void' (śūnya-sampādane) unfolds as a debate on devotion, work, powers, renunciation and realization.

attribution.tradition: the recorded discourse of the śaraṇas at the Anubhava Maṇṭapa
attribution.scholarly: compiled in four successive redactions in the Vijayanagara period (15th–16th c.) from twelfth-century vacanas and linking prose

structure.description: four redactions; the fourth (Gūḷūra Siddhavīraṇṇoḍeya) is the standard edited text, arranged in chapters (sampādane); chapter counts differ by redaction

editions.name: S. S. Bhoosnurmath (ed.), with English translation by Bhoosnurmath and Armando Menezes, Karnatak University, Dharwad, 5 vols. (1965–1972) — confirm

notes: Some accounts speak of five versions; four named compilers are recorded here.

title: Śūnyasampādane — first redaction (Śivagaṇaprasādi Mahādēvayya)
summary: One of the successive redactions of the Śūnyasampādane, rearranging and extending the vacana dialogues centred on Allama Prabhu.
notes: Recorded as a redaction of src:sunyasampadane via part_of. Order of redactions as commonly given; dates low confidence.

title: Śūnyasampādane — redaction of Halageyārya
summary: One of the successive redactions of the Śūnyasampādane, rearranging and extending the vacana dialogues centred on Allama Prabhu.
notes: Recorded as a redaction of src:sunyasampadane via part_of. Order of redactions as commonly given; dates low confidence.

title: Śūnyasampādane — redaction of Gummaḷāpurada Siddhaliṅgayati
summary: One of the successive redactions of the Śūnyasampādane, rearranging and extending the vacana dialogues centred on Allama Prabhu.
notes: Recorded as a redaction of src:sunyasampadane via part_of. Order of redactions as commonly given; dates low confidence.

title: Śūnyasampādane — redaction of Gūḷūra Siddhavīraṇṇoḍeya
summary: One of the successive redactions of the Śūnyasampādane, rearranging and extending the vacana dialogues centred on Allama Prabhu.
notes: Recorded as a redaction of src:sunyasampadane via part_of. Order of redactions as commonly given; dates low confidence.

title: Basava Purāṇamu (Pālkuriki Sōmanātha)
summary: A Telugu purāṇa in dvipada couplets narrating Basava's life, his devotion to Śiva's devotees, the miracles of the śaraṇas and of earlier (purātana) Śaiva saints, and the events at Kalyāṇa; the earliest full-scale hagiography of Basava.

scholarly.text: 13th c. (Pālkuriki Sōmanātha's dates are debated: late 12th to late 13th c.)

title: Paṇḍitārādhya Caritra (Pālkuriki Sōmanātha)
summary: A Telugu hagiography of Mallikārjuna Paṇḍitārādhya, the Andhra Śaiva teacher contemporary with Basava, including much lore of Śaiva devotees and of Śrīśaila.

title: Vṛṣādhipa Śatakamu
summary: A Telugu century of verses by Pālkuriki Sōmanātha in praise of Basava as Nandin (Vṛṣādhipa) incarnate.

title: Śivatattvasāra (Mallikārjuna Paṇḍitārādhya)
summary: A verse work on Śiva-devotion and the conduct of devotees ascribed to Mallikārjuna Paṇḍitārādhya.
notes: Language (Telugu) and content from memory; verify.

title: Basavapurāṇa (Bhīmakavi)
summary: A Kannada rendering in ṣaṭpadi verse (1369) of Pālkuriki Sōmanātha's Telugu Basava Purāṇa, the classic Kannada narrative of Basava's life and of the śaraṇas.

title: Basavapurāṇa (Sanskrit)
summary: An extended Sanskrit narrative of the life and deeds of Basava, printed in 1905 with an ascription to Bādarāyaṇa (Vyāsa).

attribution.tradition: ascribed to Bādarāyaṇa (Vyāsa) in the printed edition

title: Basavarājadēvara Ragaḷe (Harihara)
summary: The earliest extant Kannada biography of Basava, in ragaḷe verse: his refusal of the sacred thread, his devotion at Kūḍalasaṅgama, his service to devotees at Kalyāṇa and his end.

title: Prabhudēvara Ragaḷe (Harihara)
summary: Harihara's ragaḷe life of Allama Prabhu: the temple drummer of Baḷḷigāve, his grief, his meeting with the yogi Animiṣa who gives him the liṅga, and his wandering as an awakened one.

title: Mahādēviyakkana Ragaḷe (Harihara)
summary: Harihara's ragaḷe life of Akka Mahādēvi: her devotion to Cennamallikārjuna, departure from the king's household, arrival at Kalyāṇa and journey to Śrīśaila.

title: Girijākalyāṇa (Harihara)
summary: A Kannada campū on the austerity of Pārvatī (Girijā) and her marriage to Śiva, a devotional classic of the Vīraśaiva poets.

title: Siddharāma Cāritra (Rāghavāṅka)
summary: Rāghavāṅka's ṣaṭpadi life of Siddharāma of Sonnalige: his devotion to Mallikārjuna, his public works, his meeting with Allama and his realization.

title: Sōmanātha Cāritra (Rāghavāṅka)
summary: Rāghavāṅka's poem on the Śaiva devotee Ādayya of Puligere and his contest with the Jainas.

title: Hariścandra Kāvya (Rāghavāṅka)
summary: Rāghavāṅka's ṣaṭpadi retelling of King Hariścandra's trials for the sake of truth; a classic of the Vīraśaiva poets, though not a doctrinal Vīraśaiva work.

title: Prabhuliṅgalīle (Cāmarasa)
summary: Cāmarasa's bhāminī-ṣaṭpadi poem presenting Allama Prabhu as Śiva's descent: Pārvatī's Māyā sent to seduce him fails, Gorakṣa's adamantine body meets Allama's void body, Siddharāma and Muktāyakka are awakened, and Allama joins the śaraṇas at Kalyāṇa before his final union at Kadaḷi (Śrīśaila).

scholarly.text: c. 1430 (court of Dēvarāya II of Vijayanagara)

editions.name: Sanskrit Prabhuliṅgalīlā (print 1903; Muktabodha M00621) — see src:prabhulingalila-sanskrit

notes: Rendered into Tamil in the 17th c. (Turaimaṅkalam Śivaprakāśar's Pirapuliṅkalīlai, low confidence) and into Sanskrit.

title: Prabhuliṅgalīlā (Sanskrit)
summary: A Sanskrit verse rendering of the Prabhuliṅgalīle narrative of Allama Prabhu.
notes: Translator not identified here.

title: Amala Basavarāja Cāritra (Siṅgirāja)
summary: A Kannada narrative of Basava's life that catalogues his miracles (traditionally eighty-eight).

title: Śivatattvacintāmaṇi (Lakkaṇṇa Daṇḍēśa)
summary: An encyclopaedic Kannada exposition of Vīraśaiva doctrine, practice and hagiography by a minister of Dēvarāya II.

title: Vivekacintāmaṇi (Nijaguṇa Śivayōgi)
summary: Nijaguṇa Śivayōgi's Kannada encyclopaedia of Śaiva and Vīraśaiva lore — doctrine, the six sthalas, yoga, ritual, ethics and cosmology — later rendered into Sanskrit.

editions.name: Sanskrit Vivekacintāmaṇi, Vīraśaiva-liṅgi-brāhmaṇa-dharma-granthamālā no. 35 (print 1906; Muktabodha digital library e-text M00620), which states that the original was composed in Kannada by Nijaguṇa Śivayogin

title: Kaivalya Paddhati (Nijaguṇa Śivayōgi)
summary: Songs (svaravacanas) of Nijaguṇa Śivayōgi on the path to liberation (kaivalya) through Śiva-knowledge and devotion.

title: Rājaśēkharavilāsa (Ṣaḍakṣaradēva)
summary: A seventeenth-century Kannada campū narrating a Śaiva devotional legend, a classic of later Vīraśaiva poetry.

title: Vṛṣabhēndravijaya (Ṣaḍakṣaradēva)
summary: A Kannada campū on the life of Basava as Nandin (Vṛṣabhēndra) incarnate.

title: Sayings of Sarvajña (tripadis)
summary: Thousands of three-line verses (tripadi) of worldly and spiritual wisdom, criticizing caste pride, ritualism and hypocrisy and praising devotion to Śiva and honest work.
notes: Sarvajña's Vīraśaiva affiliation is itself debated; included because the tradition claims him.

title: Pirapuliṅkalīlai (Turaimaṅkalam Śivaprakāśar)
summary: A Tamil rendering of the Prabhuliṅgalīle narrative of Allama Prabhu.

title: Abalūr inscription of Ēkānta Rāmayya
summary: A Kannada stone inscription at Abalūr recording Ēkānta Rāmayya's contest with the Jainas, in which he is said to have offered his own head to Śiva and received it back, and the conversion of the Jaina shrine to Śiva's worship.
notes: The Jaina side is known here only through this Śaiva record (reported by the other side).

title: Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi
summary: The principal Sanskrit scripture of the Pañcācārya strand: the teaching of the gaṇa Reṇuka (Revaṇasiddha), who emerged from the Someśvara liṅga at Kollipāki, to the sage Agastya on the Malaya mountain. It sets out Vīraśaiva doctrine as Śivādvaita consistent with Veda and Āgama and maps the path as 101 sthalas (44 on the side of the soul, 57 on the side of the liṅga) under the six great sthalas from bhakta to aikya.

attribution.tradition: Śiva's teaching to the Goddess and Nandin, transmitted by Reṇuka to Agastya and set down by Śivayogi Śivācārya (SSM 1.28–31)
attribution.scholarly: a Sanskrit compilation by Śivayogi Śivācārya; its date is debated (placed variously between the 12th and 15th c.)

tradition.text: the teaching is anādi; Reṇuka's descent in the Kali age

structure.description: 21 chapters (pariccheda); ch. 1 frame and author's lineage; 2–4 descent of Reṇuka and meeting with Agastya; 5–14 the 44 aṅga-sthalas under bhakta (15), māheśvara (9), prasādi (7), prāṇaliṅgi (5), śaraṇa (4), aikya (4); 15–20 the 57 liṅga-sthalas; 21 Reṇuka's dialogue with Vibhīṣaṇa and his return into the liṅga

editions.name: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

notes: Chapter structure, sthala lists and all SSM refs used by this unit were checked against the local e-text (sources_raw/raw_etexts/mixed/mukta/vIrashaiva/…/siddhAntashikhAmaNi__M00207.md). family 'vedic' follows the coverage-map grouping (A7, Vedic family); it does not settle the tradition's internal debate on Vedic authority (see dsp:virasaiva-veda-agama-authority).

title: Tattvapradīpikā (Maritoṇṭadārya's commentary on the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi)
summary: A Sanskrit commentary glossing the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi verse by verse with supporting quotations from Veda, Upaniṣad, Āgama and Purāṇa; its introduction links Śivayogi to the lineage of Siddharāma and Revaṇasiddha and it names the 'world-famous Pañcācārya lineage'.

editions.name: Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna, Vārāṇasī 2006, with Maritoṇṭadārya's Tattvapradīpikā (Muktabodha e-text M00207)

title: Vīraśaivānandacandrikā (Maritoṇṭadārya)
summary: A large Sanskrit compendium of Vīraśaiva doctrine and practice that opens by setting Mahāliṅga, 'in harmony (samarasa) with its own inconceivable non-different power', above the ultimates of the other schools.

title: Liṅgadhāraṇacandrikā (Nandikeśvara)
summary: A Sanskrit treatise defending the wearing of the liṅga on the body (liṅgadhāraṇa) with quotations from Veda, Āgama and Purāṇa.

editions.name: Muktabodha digital library e-text M00333 (print 1905, with commentary by Śivakumāraśāstrin)

title: Kriyāsāra (Nīlakaṇṭha)
summary: A Sanskrit Vīraśaiva work in verse, edited in two volumes by the Oriental Research Institute, Mysore (1954), with a separate commentary (Tattvaprakāśinī of Nārāyaṇa).

editions.name: N. S. Venkatanathacharya (ed.), ORI Mysore Sanskrit Series 95 & 99, 1954 (Muktabodha digital library e-text M00118, M00050)

notes: Commonly described as a Vīraśaiva recasting of Śrīkaṇṭha's Brahmasūtra doctrine — low confidence; verify.

title: Vīraśaivācārakaustubha (Maunappa Paṇḍita)
summary: A Sanskrit manual of Vīraśaiva conduct (ācāra) for those devoted to its observances.

title: Vīraśaivotkarṣapradīpikā
summary: A Sanskrit tract on the pre-eminence of Vīraśaiva dharma, printed as the work of Cennabasaveśvara.

title: Anādivīraśaivasārasaṅgraha
summary: A Sanskrit compendium of the 'beginningless' Vīraśaiva dharma that opens with homage to Guru Basava-liṅga and to Prabhu (Allama).

title: Vīraśaivācārapradīpikā
summary: A Sanskrit manual of Vīraśaiva conduct including a section on initiation (dīkṣā) and its proper time and place, framed as Śiva's answers to Pārvatī.

title: Vedāntasāra-Vīraśaiva-Cintāmaṇi
summary: A Sanskrit work presenting Vīraśaiva teaching as the essence of Vedānta; it quotes the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi on uniting the iṣṭaliṅga and the prāṇaliṅga.

title: Śivādvaitamañjarī
summary: A Sanskrit Śivādvaita treatise, printed with related Vīraśaiva works (the catalogue title names Svaprabhānanda and a Śaivasiddhāntadīpikā).

title: Śivādvaitadarpaṇa
summary: A Sanskrit Śivādvaita treatise by an author styled paramahaṃsa-parivrājakācārya, catalogued as a Vīraśaiva text.

title: Vīraśaivasiddhāntottarakaumudī
summary: A Sanskrit ritual manual (paddhati) of Vīraśaiva worship containing a complete Śiva-pūjā-vidhi.

editions.name: Muktabodha digital library e-text M00604, M00605

title: Kaivalyasāra (Toṇṭadārya)
summary: An exposition of the 101 sthalas with strings of Vedic (śruti) quotations, styled 'awakener to the supreme Vīraśaiva non-duality', by the renunciant teacher Toṇṭadārya.

editions.name: Muktabodha digital library e-text M00602 (print 1907, Vīraśaiva-liṅgi-brāhmaṇa-dharma-granthamālā no. 30)

notes: Colophon: 'ekottaraśatasthala-śrutimālā-vivaraṇa'.

title: Śivasiddhāntacandrikā (Siddhanañjeśa Śivācārya)
summary: A Sanskrit dialogue on Śaiva doctrine opening with homage to Śiva as the liṅga of the thirty-six tattvas and the brahman of the six sthalas.

editions.name: Muktabodha digital library e-text M00617 (print 1920; verses only)

title: Viśeṣārthaprakāśikā
summary: A Sanskrit guru–disciple dialogue presented as part of a 'Śivasiddhāntatantra', on the agency of Śiva in the devotee's actions and related Vīraśaiva doctrine.

title: Vīracūḍāmaṇi
summary: A Sanskrit text catalogued among Vīraśaiva works; contents not yet summarized in this skeleton.

title: Vīratantra
summary: A short Sanskrit Vīraśaiva text that opens with homage to Mahāliṅga and to the jaṅgama teacher Toṇṭada Siddha.

title: Vīraśaivāgama
summary: A Sanskrit āgama arranged in six chapters (paṭala) by the six sthalas, from bhakta to śivaliṅgaikya.

title: Candrajñānāgama (Vīraśaiva recension)
summary: The Vīraśaiva recension of the Candrajñāna Āgama (kriyā- and caryā-pāda), one of the Āgamas the tradition reads as teaching Vīraśaiva dharma in its later portion.
notes: Distinct from the Śaiva Siddhānta transmission of the Candrajñāna (U08).

title: Makuṭāgama (Vīraśaiva recension)
summary: The kriyā- and caryā-pāda of the Makuṭa Āgama in its Vīraśaiva recension, published by the Śaivabhāratī Śodhapratiṣṭhāna of the Jaṅgamavāḍī maṭha, Vārāṇasī.

title: Vātulottara (Vātulāgama tradition)
summary: An Āgama of the Vātula group — the last of the twenty-eight Āgamas 'from Kāmika to Vātula' that the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi names as its scriptural base (SSM 1.25).

title: Śivatattvaratnākara (Keḷadi Basavarāja)
summary: An encyclopaedic Sanskrit work by the Vīraśaiva ruler of Keḷadi covering Śaiva doctrine, ritual, the arts, statecraft and cosmology.

title: Anubhavasūtra (Māyidēva)
summary: A Sanskrit sūtra-style exposition of the ṣaṭsthala path and the union of liṅga and aṅga.
notes: Reconstructed from memory; verify existence, author and date.

title: Śivayogapradīpikā
summary: A Sanskrit manual that joins liṅga-devotion with the yoga of mantra, laya, haṭha and rāja as 'Śivayoga'.
notes: Author (a Vīraśaiva Sadāśiva/Cennasadāśiva Yogi?) and date not recalled with confidence; verify before use.

title: Bhagavadgītā Vīraśaiva-bhāṣya (T. G. Siddappārādhya)
summary: A twentieth-century commentary on the Bhagavad Gītā from the Vīraśaiva standpoint.
